### workspace hooks --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace hooks <subcommand> [options]

Manage the hooks workspace installs into coding agents' own settings
('workspace init', 'start' and 'doctor --fix' install them).

Subcommands:
  uninstall   Remove workspace's hooks for one agent, keeping your own

Examples:
  workspace hooks uninstall --agent codex --dry-run    # see what would go from Codex's hooks.json
  workspace hooks uninstall --agent codex    # remove workspace's Codex hooks, keeping your own
  workspace hooks uninstall --agent claude --project --dry-run    # preview a clean-up of every checkout of this project
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace hooks uninstall --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace hooks uninstall --agent KIND [--name WS | --project [NAME]] [--dry-run] [--json]

Remove workspace's hooks from KIND's settings file: Codex's
$CODEX_HOME/hooks.json (default ~/.codex/hooks.json), or for claude
the .claude/settings.json of the current directory's project, or of
the checkouts --name or --project pick. Only handlers running
'workspace session-event' go; your own hooks and every other key stay.
The file is backed up first. Running it again changes nothing.
'workspace init', 'start' or 'doctor --fix' install them again.

Options:
        --agent KIND                 The agent whose hooks to remove: codex or claude
        --name WS                    claude: the checkout of workspace WS, not the current directory
        --project [NAME]             claude: every checkout of the project (main and worktrees); NAME is a project,
                                     a path in it or a member workspace, default the current directory's
        --dry-run                    Say what would be removed, and change nothing
        --json                       Print one action document (exit 3 when some checkouts failed)

Examples:
  workspace hooks uninstall --agent codex --dry-run    # see what would go from Codex's hooks.json first
  workspace hooks uninstall --agent codex    # stop Codex reporting to workspace, keeping your own hooks
  workspace hooks uninstall --agent claude --name my-feature    # clean up one workspace's checkout
  workspace hooks uninstall --agent claude --project --dry-run    # preview every checkout of this project
  workspace hooks uninstall --agent=codex --json    # a script removing the hooks and reading the outcome
--- stderr
--- end
